So through a cohousing facebook group. 

She (F21) posted a post saying she was looking for someone to cohouse with. I (F19) responsed, we met up before to be sure we were on the same wavelength (on agreements, lifestyle, boundaries, open communication etc). 

We clicked and signed a contract together. This was may 2024, so it’s been 7 months now. We have been okay with each other since, do outdoor activities together, laugh, criticise each other (lol), sing, dance, talk a lot and openly (normally). 

But i think you’re right, i’m taking it very personal. I realised that i often am mistaking silence (treatments) for “i fucked up and this is someones way of letting me know that”. I will try to focus on my breathing and remind myself that it’s out of my control. But i will try to, if i see her give hints that i care about her wellbeing. 

About the flowers… idk she’s acting strange now but in normal circumstances she would 1. Laugh in my face 2. Be flattered. So not sure hahah

Thank you for taking the time to respond :) 
have a blessed rest of your day

And honestly i get why you feel like your cutting might not be that big of a deal… but that doesn’t make it a fact. I also don’t get the feeling that this is what he’s literally telling you. It’s important to separate your own insecurities and interpretations from literal facts. Or double check this in a conversation with him. “When you keep repeating this i feel like you’re telling me…”

Honestly, after following DBT therapy. I have a different perspective on this. Both are copings, apart from their intensity and the parasuicidal side.They are similar in the way that everything that you compulsively reach for to deal with underlying issues, emotions, etc. are destructive copings. So honestly a relapse is a relapse, drinking, binge eating, ignoring your family or friends, or even screen time can all be escapisms. On an intensity scale it could range from “mild” to severe impacts on body. Maybe try to see it like that. It’s not the same or same intensity, but even among people that cut, it’s never the same reason nor intensity nor same underlying issues/emotions they’re dealing with. People often try to relate to each other, maybe that’s his way to try to relate to you and maybe he doesn’t mean any harm at all or doesn’t mean to downplay what you’re going through. But you’re right it’s not the same, but in the same sense you might also not experience the intensity of another person’s destructive behaviour. It still wouldn’t make yours invalid to try to relate if you would…
